acceptance_checks: A PR with locks ['path:docs/**'] and a rename status entry from tests/ to docs/ blocks with 'outside declared task locks', identical to the delete+add form.
A rename entirely inside the declared locks still returns ready (no false positive).
A PR for goal G-A deleting .shiki/dag/G-B.json blocks, both with and without --base-shiki.
Modifying or deleting a foreign .shiki/reports, plans, runs, worktrees, memories or runner record blocks; the PR's own goal/task-scoped records in those directories still pass.
A PR touching .shiki/schemas/cca-verdict.schema.json under locks ['path:.shiki/schemas/**'] returns ready.
.shiki/somewhere/cca-verdict.json and .shiki/somewhere/mergegate-result.json still block (the anti-forgery guard in test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh stays green).
A PR adding a new .shiki/plans record that is not the current goal's source_plan is blocked.
A PR that adds a spec_freeze block to its own goal's source plan is blocked.
A PR that modifies an existing spec_freeze block — including appending to amendments — is blocked.
A PR that touches its own goal's plan without altering spec_freeze is unaffected.

findings.detail: In enforce_untrusted_shiki_mutations the per-candidate loop checks both the D-leg entry's path and the A-leg entry's old_path for a rename, so a renamed forbidden/runtime path can be reported twice. Cosmetic only — no incorrect verdict.
findings.title: Rename old path can produce duplicate blocking messages

findings.detail: _mirror_record_scoped blocks a synced mirror record whose stem is not the task/goal id and whose content carries neither matching goal_id nor task_id. Intended anti-padding/fail-closed behavior, and real scorecard reports and runner EXEC records carry goal_id/task_id, but it is a latent false-positive risk if any future mirror writer omits those ids on a record the loop syncs onto a task branch.
findings.title: Mirror records lacking goal_id/task_id and not id-named fail closed

scope: In scripts/mergegate_check.py: (a) derive the lock-scope path set from files_status (which already decomposes a rename into D(old)+A(new)) and pass it to both files_outside_locks and active_lock_conflicts, so a rename cannot move a file out of locked scope unseen; (b) add a generic mirror-class rule covering the eleven unscoped directories (dag, plans, reports, memories, runs, worktrees, handoffs, runner, smoke, starts, inbox) — block deletion and require goal/task scoping — and extend the base-snapshot delete-protection loop to every tracked mirror directory in the manifest; (c) match the exact runtime filenames cca-verdict.json and mergegate-result.json in runtime_evidence_path() instead of a startswith prefix, which today makes .shiki/schemas/cca-verdict.schema.json permanently unmergeable. Additionally, forbid a PR from creating or modifying a spec_freeze block in ANY mirror state, including its own goal's source plan. Goal/task scoping alone is not sufficient: it stops a PR from writing a foreign plan, but still lets an implementation PR grant itself a Spec Freeze, or append amendments, on the plan that governs it. Spec Freeze is operator-only (ADR 0009), so no PR may author the record of it.
test_command: bash scripts/test_shiki_adversarial_state.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_state_classes.sh && bash scripts/test_shiki_control_plane.sh && python3 -m unittest discover -s tests
title: Make MergeGate scope enforcement see the whole diff and the whole mirror
